L57: Seasonal Influenza Vaccine (mRNA-1010): In August, Moderna received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for mFLUSIVA®, its seasonal influenza vaccine, for adults aged 50–64 years and accelerated approval for adults aged 65 years and older, marking the Company's fifth approved product globally. Moderna is conducting a limited U.S. launch for the 2026–2027 influenza season, with approval occurring after the annual contracting cycle. The Company also received approval for mFLUSIVA in Canada.
L58: Flu/COVID Combination Vaccine (mRNA-1083): Moderna received regulatory approval in Canada for mCOFLU®, the Company's flu/COVID combination vaccine, following approval of the vaccine under the brand name mCOMBRIAX® in the European Union. The vaccine remains under regulatory review in additional markets, including Japan, the United Kingdom and Australia. Moderna continues to await further guidance from the FDA regarding refiling in the United States.
L59: Norovirus Vaccine (mRNA-1403): Following the Phase 3 interim analysis, which did not meet the statistical criteria for early success, Moderna does not plan to initiate an additional cohort this season. The Company intends to engage with health authorities to determine the program's path forward.

L61: Oncology Therapeutics
L62: Intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157): In October, Moderna and Merck presented positive Phase 3 results from the INTerpath-001 study in resected high-risk melanoma at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026. Intismeran autogene in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% (HR=0.58) and the risk of distant metastasis or death by 38% (HR=0.62), compared with KEYTRUDA alone, in the intention-to-treat population.
L63: The benefit was greater after six months, following the intismeran immunization regimen, as intismeran plus KEYTRUDA reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 58% (piecewise HR=0.42 [95% CI, 0.30–0.58]) compared to KEYTRUDA alone in a pre-specified sensitivity analysis. Moderna and Merck are working toward regulatory submissions and preparing for a potential commercial launch, subject to regulatory approval.
L64: mRNA-4359: Moderna continues Phase 2 clinical trial of its investigational cancer antigen therapy in first-line metastatic melanoma, previously treated metastatic melanoma and first-line non-small cell lung cancer.

L66: mRNA-2808: Abstract accepted for oral presentation at American Society of Hematology meeting on December 12th in New Orleans.

L79: Moderna Corporate Updates
L80: •Leadership Appointment: In September, Moderna announced the appointment of Juan Andres as Chief Operating Officer, effective October 5, 2026. Mr. Andres previously served in senior leadership positions at Moderna and will oversee the Company's operational strategy and execution, including its global manufacturing organization.
L81: 
L82: •Leadership Retirement: In September, Moderna announced that Jerh Collins, Ph.D., Chief Technical Operations and Quality Officer, retired following four years with the Company.
L83: •Financing: In September, Moderna completed a convertible senior notes offering totaling approximately $3.0 billion in principal amount. After accounting for the purchase of capped calls designed to mitigate potential future dilution and associated fees, we raised approximately $2.6 billion in net proceeds. The financing provides additional financial flexibility to support continued investment in oncology and address future debt obligations.
L84: •Litigation Settlement: Moderna and GSK entered into an agreement on October 28, 2026, to settle all disputes between the parties which were pending in the U.S. and Europe. Pursuant to the agreement, the parties granted patent cross-licenses in the field of infectious disease and are not obligated to make payments of any kind in connection with such licenses.
